notes: Live research 14 Oct 2026. AU EGLS is American University's most prestigious UNDERGRADUATE merit scholarship, administered entirely by the Office of Enrollment / International Admissions - no faculty member supervises, selects, or is attached to it. Official AU page (https://www.american.edu/admissions/international/au-egls-apply.cfm): 'The AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS) promotes educational access and opportunity while enhancing international diversity... The AU EGLS covers all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room, and board) for two international students who will need a non-immigrant visa'; 'If you have any questions, please contact intadm@american.edu'. Selection is by 'Zoom interviews and/or additional essay submissions' run by admissions staff; the award is open to 'any major offered at AU'. No professor, lab, or research-group tie exists, so supervisor enrichment is not applicable by nature. Transparency note: direct fetch of the official page returned HTTP 403 (bot protection) on 14 Oct 2026; the page content above was confirmed through the live search index of the same american.edu URL, and the award's undergraduate, admissions-administered character was corroborated by AU's ISSS page (https://www.american.edu/student-affairs/isss/scholarships-for-international-students.cfm): 'A separate application is required only for the AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship'.

Live research 14 Oct 2026. The Jefferson Scholarship is a nominative UNDERGRADUATE merit award of the Jefferson Scholars Foundation at the University of Virginia; it funds four years of bachelor's study and has no supervising professor. Official Foundation page (https://www.jeffersonscholars.org/scholarships): the Foundation 'attracts outstanding undergraduate students to the University of Virginia through two scholarship programs - the Jefferson Scholars Program and the Walentas Scholars Program' and covers 'the entire cost of attendance for four years'. Selection (https://www.jeffersonscholars.org/scholarships/selection) is run by a nominating-school/alumni pipeline, not faculty: 'Regional Selection Committees - comprised of alumni and friends of the University - review transcripts, extracurricular activities, essays, and recommendations', and 'The Jefferson Scholars Foundation is separate from the Office of Undergraduate Admission'. Faculty appear only in the Foundation's separate Distinguished Professorship Program and Faculty Awards (https://www.jeffersonscholars.org/faculty-support), which fund/recognise UVA professors and are not supervision of scholarship recipients. Research collaboration is with 'Jefferson Fellows' (graduate fellows), not with a named supervising professor. Not applicable by nature.

The King-Morgridge Scholars Program (KMSP) is a four-year/eight-semester UNDERGRADUATE full-tuition scholarship at UW-Madison housed in the International Division, with staff (not faculty) oversight. Staff page (https://kmsp.wisc.edu/staff/) names the programme leadership: Kate McCleary, 'Associate Dean of Academic Initiatives, International Division', who 'oversees the operations of the King-Morgridge Scholars Program and serves as a mentor to the scholars' (institutional profile: https://eps.education.wisc.edu/staff/mccleary-kate/), and Jay Stokes, 'Program Manager of King-Morgridge Scholars Program'; application questions go to kmscholars@admissions.wisc.edu. These are programme administrators, not supervising professors, and an undergraduate merit scholarship has no thesis/PHD supervision, so supervisor enrichment is not applicable by nature.

Official Brandeis ISSO page (https://www.brandeis.edu/isso/programs/wien/index.html): 'The Wien International Scholarship Program (WISP) at Brandeis University, established in 1958, is a first-of-its-kind program bringing undergraduate students from every corner of the globe to campus'; the page lists current Wien Scholars by name and country only, and directs contact to 'International Students and Scholars Office, Gerstenzang 136, MS 040, Brandeis University... isso@brandeis.edu'. notes: Live research 14 Oct 2026. Knight-Hennessy Scholars is a graduate fellowship, not a single-department PhD programme: 'All scholars are Stanford University graduate students, who join Knight-Hennessy Scholars in addition to enrolling in a graduate degree program at any of Stanford's seven schools' (https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu). Funding: 'Scholars receive a fellowship for up to three years of tuition, depending upon their degree length. In addition, scholars receive a stipend for living and academic expenses, and a travel stipend' (https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/about-knight-hennessy-scholars/overview-knight-hennessy-scholars). Because a scholar's thesis supervisor sits in whichever Stanford department/programme they are admitted to, the only faculty ties published by the programme itself are (a) its leadership - co-founder/Shriram Family Director John Hennessy and Executive Director Tina Seelig - and (b) the KHS Faculty Fellows, a published cross-school panel (Roland Greene, Stephanie Harman, Lerone A. Martin, Christine Ngaruiya, Jelena Obradovic, Nathaniel Persily, Rob Reich, Janine Zacharia, Matt Abrahams, etc.). The three professors recorded above are the leadership plus the engineering Faculty Fellow most useful for research-supervision outreach; other Faculty Fellows are listed at https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/about-knight-hennessy-scholars/faculty-fellows. Also noted: a KHS news release (https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/news/mariano-florentino-tino-cuellar-joins-knight-hennessy-scholars-shriram-family-director) announces Mariano-Florentino 'Tino' Cuellar as the incoming Shriram Family Director succeeding Hennessy, who moves to the KHS Advisory Board while 'remaining involved in teaching and advising scholars'. No email addresses are published for Hennessy or Seelig on any stanford.edu page, so their official_email fields are null.
